questions.stem: "Once I've used it, I can still use it after a month away." Which usability goal is this?
questions.explanation: Memorability is how easy it is to remember how to use a product after a break; learnability is how easy it is to learn in the first place (Slide 3).
questions.hint: It is about remembering, not learning.

questions.stem: Which is a user experience goal rather than a usability goal?
questions.explanation: User experience goals describe how the interaction feels (enjoyable, satisfying); efficiency, safety and learnability are usability goals (Slides 3–4).

questions.stem: Which is NOT one of the four interaction design activities?
questions.explanation: The four activities are discover requirements, design alternatives, prototype and evaluate, repeated iteratively (Slide 5).
questions.hint: Three of these appear on Slide 5.

questions.stem: Which principle of user-centred design means testing designs with real people and changing them?
questions.explanation: User-centred design combines an early focus on users, empirical measurement of real use, and iteration (Slide 6).
